articles.title: Lions shaken after All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell taken to hospital with ‘scary’ neck injury
articles.summary: 26-year-old injured making tackle in fourth quarter. Linebacker treated for nearly 10 minutes on field. Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell sustained a neck injury and was taken to a local ⁠hospital after being injured during the fourth quarter of his team’s 19-15 victory over the Minnesota…
body: “Thoughts and ⁠prayers are ​with Jack and his family,” Lions head coach Dan Campbell said after the game. “He’s being ⁠taken care of. We don’t have any new information. We’ll keep you updated as this thing goes. But ⁠we are thinking about him. We are thinking about him.”
The Lions later said that Campbell would be kept in hospital overnight.

“Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring,” the Lions said in a statement. “The team will provide further updates as we have them.”
Jack Campbell, ​a first-team All-Pro last ‌season, was injured while ‌tackling Vikings tight end TJ Hockenson in the fourth quarter.

articles.title: European football: Mbappé penalty helps Real Madrid stroll to sixth straight win
articles.summary: Bellingham and Diomandé complete 3-0 win over Racing. Lazio top Serie A after fighting back to beat Cagliari. Kylian Mbappé moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.
body: The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.
Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.
Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomandé were also on target to keep third-placed Madrid within three points of the La Liga leaders, Barcelona, who thrashed Alavés 6-1 on Saturday.
José Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind Atlético Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.

articles.title: ‘He’s done an insane job’: Antonelli’s rivals unite in praise for F1’s youngest champion
articles.summary: Lando Norris: ‘People are not giving him enough credit’ 20-year-old sealed F1 title after finishing third in Mexico. Formula One’s leading drivers have been unstinting in their praise for the new champion, Kimi Antonelli, after the Italian driver took his debut title with third place at the Mexican…
body: Antonelli became the youngest world champion at 20 years old in Mexico, sharing a podium with race winner Max Verstappen and second-placed Lewis Hamilton. He has taken the title in only his second year in the sport after a remarkable season including nine wins.

“It’s a special moment,” said Antonelli. “One that we’ll remember for ever.” While his race engineer, Peter Bonnington, suggested this may well be the first of many. “It’s a ­pleasure to be on the journey with you, but it’s just the first chapter,” he said.
The defending champion, Lando Norris, led what were fulsome ­tributes to the driver who had taken his crown, emphasising that he felt Antonelli had been exceptional.

“He’s done an insane job. I feel like people are not giving him enough credit for what he’s achieved this year,” said Norris. “He’s beaten the teammate that’s been in the sport for four times longer than him. Who was also very good and who took the battle to Lewis Hamilton.”

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion with third place in Mexican GP
articles.summary: 20-year-old clinches title with four races to go. Verstappen wins race ahead of Hamilton. Kimi Antonelli etched his name into the Formula One record books as world champion and as a deserved and popular winner whose verve and extraordinary skill has been thrilling to watch, turning what many…
body: In taking his debut F1 title for Mercedes, the 20-year-old Antonelli, with his tousled hair and charming boyish looks, is the youngest driver to claim the sport’s crown and the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari won in 1953. It is Mercedes’ first drivers’ championship since Hamilton last won in 2020 and the team’s 10th.

The youngster closed it out unsurprisingly with the cool command the greats of the sport display by taking third place in Mexico City, a race won after no little drama by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, from the ­Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton, who was left fuming with his teammate Charles Leclerc, who finished fourth.

Afterwards Antonelli was clearly moved and said it was a moment that would live for ever but had left him almost speechless. His race engineer, Peter Bonnington, spoke perhaps for everyone who has watched the Italian this season, noting that this was just the beginning for Antonelli.
“It is a very special day, a young man has broken the record for the youngest world champion,” he said. “It is the first of many I reckon, I am just super happy for him, stoked.”

articles.title: Defensive 'masterclass' and elite Rice - how Arsenal ended Anfield torment
articles.summary: Not since 2012 - when current boss Mikel Arteta was commanding Arsenal's midfield on the pitch - had the Gunners won on Liverpool’s patch. That curse has finally been broken.
body: Winning at Anfield is a rarity, especially for Arsenal. But Arteta's side were ruthless at both ends of the pitch, a tactical triumph for the boss and one that underlines his side's champion mentality.

"I love when there is something that we haven't done for many years," beamed the Spaniard, who praised his players for a defensive performance he called "remarkable". If Arteta wanted to make a statement, he succeeded.

Despite being pinned back in a first half dominated by Liverpool pressure, the visitors restricted their hosts to zero accurate shots - the first time on record the Reds failed to land at least one attempt on target at home.

"In the end, that defensive line, the way we stick together, that togetherness we have, is undefeated," midfielder Declan Rice reflected. "It's nothing I've ever seen before." Nine games in, Arsenal's title defence is going perfectly to plan.

articles.title: Antonelli crowned world champion as Verstappen wins wild Mexico City GP
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history as Max Verstappen held off Lewis Hamilton to win a thrilling Mexico City Grand Prix.
body: Antonelli finished third to secure the F1 Drivers' Championship with four rounds to spare, becoming the first Italian world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
The 20-year-old avoided all the chaos in one of the most action-packed races of the season and was hugely emotional after the chequered flag.
"We did it, we did it. I wouldn't be here without Mercedes, without my family, so I'm very grateful for this moment and it's one that will live forever," said Antonelli.
Meanwhile, Verstappen took advantage of a big fight between the Ferraris of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc on the opening lap to claim his third win in four races.

articles.title: Ravens QB Jackson to undergo surgery in new injury setback
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson will undergo surgery on his right thumb and miss at least the next four games on injured reserve, Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed on Sunday.
body: Jackson suffered the injury on his first play from scrimmage in Baltimore's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills when his throwing hand was hit by pass rusher Greg Rousseau.
Minter announced afterwards that the two-time MVP would be placed on injured reserve, adding "we'll see" when asked if the issue might prove to be season-ending.
Jackson had been making his return to action for one of the biggest matchups of the season after missing the last three games with a high ankle sprain.
Matters were made worse when backup quarterback Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the first half, resulting in undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano coming in as the emergency third-choice.

articles.title: Chicago Cubs news: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Alex Bregman win Gold Gloves
articles.summary: The Rawlings Gold Glove Awards were announced tonight and two Cubs players, center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman, came home with the trophies. It was the second-straight win in center field for Crow-Armstrong.
body: Josiah Hartshorn, the Cubs’ top prospect, also won a minor league Gold Glove as the top defensive first baseman across all of the minor leagues.

Crow-Armstrong beat the Dodgers’ Andy Pages and the Braves’ Michael Harris for the award in center field. Bregman topped the Dodgers’ Max Muncy and the Marlins’ Javier Sanoja for the honors at third base.

Three other Cubs were finalists for a Gold Glove, but came up short. Ian Happ, who has won the Gold Glove in each of the past four seasons, lost this time to the Brewers Jackson Chourio. Right fielder Seiya Suzuki was among the top three in right field, but the award went to the Diamondbacks’ Corbin Carroll. Shortstop Dansby Swanson, who won the award twice with Atlanta, lost out to the D-Backs’ Geraldo Perdomo.
There is still the Platinum Glove Award to be given out, and you can vote for Crow-Armstrong or Bregman at Rawlings dot com.
